faq.a: Badai is associated with the Arabic form بديع, whose core sense is majestic, glorious.

faq.q: What is the origin of Badai?
faq.a: Badai is associated with Arabic. Badīʿ ('marvellous, original'); al-Badīʿ is one of the divine names. The source record's gloss 'Majestic, Glorious' is an approximation.
Yes — the underlying form بديع is Arabic.
Badai can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Badai should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. البديع is a name of God in the Qur'an (2:117)

faq.a: Romanization variants include Badai, badai. Script forms are بديع, بدیع, बदाई.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
